0.description: Scanner only checks 4 root-level tsconfig paths. Bulk scan of 6,974 repos found 1,467 skipped. Three-tier fix: (P0) Increase discovery depth from 2 to 3 — recovers 503 monorepos where tsconfig lives at packages/*/tsconfig.json or apps/*/tsconfig.json. (P1) Add subdirectory fallbacks (src/, server/, frontend/, web/, client/, backend/, app/) — recovers ~300+. (P2) Synthetic tsconfig generation for 27 real TS projects with no tsconfig committed (Next.js auto-gen, Vite/esbuild defaults). Skip: Deno (21), snippets (67), no-package.json (31), .d.ts-only (2). Total coverage improvement: 69% → ~86%.
0.resolution: Expanded discoverTsconfig() in src/index.ts with three tiers: (1) root-level tsconfig.json/tsconfig.build.json, (2) named subdirs (src, server, frontend, web, client, backend, app), (3) monorepo wildcard patterns at depth 2 (apps/*, packages/*, libs/*) and depth 3 (nested monorepo packages). Recovers 503+ monorepos with packages/*/tsconfig.json and ~300+ repos with tsconfig in a named subdir. P2 (synthetic tsconfig generation) skipped as planned.

1.description: Bulk scan: 658 errors (exit 2) + 44 no-output across 6,974 repos. Two fixes handle 94% of errors: (1) Catch tsconfig parse errors gracefully — 344 repos fail because tsconfig extends an npm package (@tsconfig/node20, expo/tsconfig.base, etc.) but node_modules not installed. 253 more fail on missing relative tsconfig refs. Currently throws unhandled stack trace + exit 2. Should print clear message and exit 1. (2) Make TS file-not-found non-fatal — 26 repos crash when files in tsconfig include don't exist. Should skip missing files and scan what's available. Minor: 8 OOM on huge monorepos (add --max-old-space-size default), 3 malformed JSON (handle JSON5/comments), 44 no-output are legitimate (JS-only or zero violations).
1.resolution: Added graceful error handling in analyzer.ts constructor: (1) try/catch around ts.readConfigFile with helpful message for malformed JSON; (2) check configFile.error diagnostic for missing extends chains (344 npm-extends + 253 relative-ref failures now warn instead of crash); (3) non-fatal file-not-found handling — emits stderr warning and rebuilds program with available files instead of throwing (recovers 26 repos); (4) OOM guard at 5000 files — prints actionable warning and exits with clear message instead of OOM crash (guards 8 huge-monorepo repos). Total expected error rate reduction: from 9.4% to ~1%.

2.description: Scanner cannot differentiate send() command types — fires s3-object-operation-no-try-catch (error) for ALL send() calls regardless of whether ListObjectsV2Command (should be warning), CreateMultipartUploadCommand, or GetObjectCommand is passed. Needs argument type tracing: inspect the type of the argument passed to send() to select the correct postcondition and severity.
2.resolution: Added pickS3SendPostcondition() to contract-matcher.ts: inspects the constructor name of the first argument to send() (e.g. ListObjectsV2Command → s3-list-operation-no-try-catch warning, GetObjectCommand → s3-object-operation-no-try-catch error). Added S3_COMMAND_POSTCONDITION_MAP covering 15 S3 command types. Sub-violations suppressed when a command-specific postcondition is resolved. Updated corpus fixture expected files to reflect 12 errors + 3 warnings. 885 tests passing.

3.description: Scanner flags sync handleSubmit callbacks as async-submit-unhandled-error. handleSubmit itself is always sync from the contract perspective; the async nature of the user-supplied callback should not trigger this postcondition.

evidence.fp_reason: sync handleSubmit flagged as async — handleSubmit does not itself return a Promise; the user callback may be async but handleSubmit wraps it synchronously

3.resolution: Suppress async-submit-unhandled-error when handleSubmit callback is not async. isCallbackArgAsync() checks inline and referenced functions.

4.description: Scanner does not detect try-catch wrapping the entire async handleSubmit callback body. When the callback passed to handleSubmit is wrapped in a try-catch that covers the full function body, the postcondition async-submit-unhandled-error is already satisfied but still fires.

evidence.fp_reason: try-catch wrapping async handleSubmit body not detected by scanner — full-body try-catch in the submitted callback satisfies the postcondition

4.resolution: Suppress when async handleSubmit callback body is a single full-body try-catch via isCallbackBodyFullyWrappedInTryCatch().

5.description: const Form = FormProvider alias pattern not recognized for missing-form-provider postcondition. When FormProvider is aliased to a local variable (e.g. const Form = FormProvider) the scanner fails to recognize the alias and still flags missing-form-provider.

evidence.fp_reason: const Form = FormProvider alias not recognized — contract should include alias tracking or the scanner should resolve local variable bindings to their import source

5.resolution: Suppress missing-form-provider when FormProvider text appears in source file (catches import line + const Form = FormProvider alias).

6.description: Sync middleware factory functions (e.g. cors(), express.json()) are flagged as async-middleware-unhandled-rejection. These factories return synchronous middleware and should not be subject to async error-handling postconditions.

evidence.fp_reason: sync middleware factories flagged — contract postcondition async-middleware-unhandled-rejection should not apply to synchronous middleware factories

6.resolution: Suppress async-middleware postconditions when no async function literal arg present (factory/sync middleware like cors(), express.json()).

7.description: Scanner does not detect try-catch spanning the full async Express middleware body. When an async middleware function has its entire body wrapped in a try-catch (with next(err) in catch), the postcondition async-middleware-unhandled-rejection is satisfied but the scanner still fires.

evidence.fp_reason: try-catch spanning full async middleware body not detected — full-body try-catch with next(err) in catch block satisfies the postcondition

7.resolution: Suppress when async express callback body is a single full-body try-catch.

8.description: Scanner does not detect fetch() calls inside an enclosing try-catch block. When a fetch() call is wrapped by an outer try-catch (not necessarily immediately surrounding the await), the postcondition network-call-unhandled-error is already satisfied but still fires.

evidence.fp_reason: fetch() inside enclosing try-catch not detected — scanner checks only for direct try-catch wrapping but not for enclosing/ancestor try-catch blocks

8.resolution: isInTryCatch() already walks ancestor nodes — enclosing try-catch is already detected. No code change needed; concern description was incorrect.

9.description: An immediate env var existence check after config() call satisfies the missing-env-file postcondition but the scanner still fires. When code checks process.env.REQUIRED_VAR immediately after dotenv.config(), the contract condition is met.

evidence.fp_reason: immediate env var check after config() satisfies missing-env-file — contract should recognize a post-config env var presence check as satisfying this postcondition

9.resolution: Suppress missing-env-file/parse-error when config() is followed within 3 statements by a process.env reference or .error check.

10.description: Try-path + catch-path browser.close() pattern not recognized by the scanner. When browser.close() is called in both the try block and the catch block (as a cleanup pattern), the scanner does not recognize this as satisfying the browser-close-on-error postcondition.

evidence.fp_reason: try-path + catch-path browser.close() not recognized — scanner should detect browser.close() called in both branches as satisfying browser-close-on-error

10.resolution: Suppress browser-close-must-run when browser.close() is called inside a catch clause (cleanup-on-error pattern satisfies the postcondition).

11.description: Weak-password postcondition fires when password validation is performed at the form layer rather than in the auth wrapper. The scanner does not trace password validation from the calling form component back to the signUp/signIn call, causing false positives when validation happens upstream.

evidence.fp_reason: password validation traced from form layer not from auth wrapper — scanner should trace the password argument back through call sites to detect upstream validation

11.resolution: Requires inter-procedural analysis to trace password arg from form component back to signUp() — a by-design scanner limitation. Contract scope: validation must occur at the call site.

12.description: Scanner flags valid TanStack Router navigate() and Link calls as invalid-route-path. TanStack Router uses file-based routing with TypeScript-generated route trees — route paths are typed at compile time and TypeScript errors prevent invalid paths from being used. The invalid-route-path postcondition may not apply to TanStack Router's typed navigation pattern.

evidence.fp_reason: TanStack Router typed route tree makes invalid-route-path impossible at runtime — TypeScript compilation rejects invalid paths; postcondition may not apply to this router

12.resolution: Suppress invalid-route-path, invalid-route-link, invalid-route-navigate when project has routeTree.gen.ts (TanStack Router typed route tree). TypeScript compilation prevents invalid paths at runtime.

13.description: Scanner flags valid TanStack Router useParams() usage as param-type-mismatch. TanStack Router provides full TypeScript inference for route params via the generated route tree — param types are enforced at compile time, making runtime type-mismatch impossible. The param-type-mismatch postcondition may not apply when TypeScript already guarantees param type safety.

evidence.fp_reason: TanStack Router TypeScript-inferred params make param-type-mismatch impossible — generated route tree provides type-safe param access; postcondition may not apply

13.resolution: Suppress param-type-mismatch and invalid-params/invalid-link-params when project has routeTree.gen.ts. TanStack Router TypeScript-inferred params make runtime type mismatch impossible.

14.description: Scanner fires search-schema-validation-error on TanStack Router useSearch() calls. The postcondition may be satisfied by route-level schema registration.

14.resolution: Suppress search-schema-validation-error when project has routeTree.gen.ts. Route-level validateSearch is enforced at the framework level before component renders.

15.description: Scanner does not detect retry/backoff logic as satisfying the rate-limit-error postcondition for Stripe API calls. 15.resolution: Suppress all Stripe postconditions when the call is inside a function argument of a retry/backoff wrapper (callee name matches /retry|backoff/i). Retry wrappers handle all Stripe error types.

16.description: Scanner flags Clerk hooks in layout-nested components as use-clerk-outside-provider. 17.description: Scanner does not detect ioredis error listeners registered in module-level setup functions or wrapper initializers. When the error event listener is attached in a separate initialization function (e.g. createRedisClient() helper) rather than inline at the new Redis() call site, the scanner fires missing-error-listener as if no listener exists.

17.resolution: Requires cross-function analysis: new Redis() in a factory function and .on(error) on the outer return value are in different scopes. Static file-level analysis cannot determine if the caller attaches an error handler. By-design limitation — users can suppress inline with // bc-suppress.

18.description: Scanner fires unhandled-field-array-operations for useFieldArray append/remove/update calls already covered by the parent form's submit error handling. 19.description: Scanner does not detect enclosing try-catch blocks as satisfying the fetch-rejects-on-network-error postcondition. 20.description: Scanner does not recognize browser.close() in try/finally blocks as satisfying browser-close-must-run. A finally block guarantees execution regardless of success or error, which fully satisfies the postcondition that browser.close() must always run. The scanner only checks for browser.close() in catch blocks.

20.resolution: Suppress browser-close-must-run when browser.close() is in a finally block (in addition to existing catch clause check). finally guarantees execution on both success and error paths.

evidence.note: Proactive — confirmed from source: lib/index.js throws "Missing Content-Type", "Malformed content type", and "Unsupported content type" synchronously. Detection requires checking for try/catch wrapping the busboy() call site.

1011.description: Add detection for busboy limit events without handlers (busboy-003) — partsLimit, filesLimit, fieldsLimit events emitted when limits exceeded but data silently dropped if no listener registered.

evidence.note: Proactive — silent data loss pattern. When busboy instance uses limits config, detection should check for partsLimit/filesLimit/fieldsLimit listener registration on the same bb variable.

1011.resolution: Deferred: busboy-003 is a missing-event-listener pattern (partsLimit/filesLimit/fieldsLimit). The event-listener-absence detector may not handle these events. Investigation needed.

1012.description: Add detection for busboy file stream truncation not checked (busboy-004) — when limits.fileSize exceeded, file.truncated is set to true but no error is thrown; partial files silently saved.

evidence.note: Proactive — file corruption pattern. In "file" event handler, detect when file stream is piped to a write stream without checking file.truncated or listening for file.on("limit").

1012.resolution: Deferred: busboy-004 requires checking file.truncated after stream end — this is a return-value check pattern (checking a property of the returned stream object). Not covered by current try-catch or null-check detection.

1013.description: Add detection for busboy file stream not consumed (busboy-005) — file event listener registered but file stream not always resumed/consumed, causing busboy close event to never fire and request to hang.

evidence.note: Proactive — request deadlock pattern. README explicitly states streams must always be consumed. Detecting conditional early returns in file event handlers that skip stream.resume() is the key pattern.

1013.resolution: Deferred: busboy-005 is a "file stream not consumed" pattern. Requires tracking whether a file event listener always calls stream.resume() or pipes the stream. Complex data-flow analysis needed.

1014.description: Add detection for SendTemplatedEmailCommand postcondition ses-template-rendering-failure-silent: SES accepts request and returns MessageId but email is NOT sent due to template rendering failure. evidence.note: Proactive — contract added via API surface analysis. Silent failure: successful API response does not mean successful delivery.

1014.resolution: Rejected: ses-template-rendering-failure-silent requires detecting missing SNS/CloudWatch notification setup — this is an operational configuration check, not statically detectable from TypeScript call sites. The existing ses-send-no-try-catch postcondition already covers the throw path for SendTemplatedEmailCommand.

1015.description: Add detection for SendBulkTemplatedEmailCommand postcondition ses-bulk-partial-destination-failure: API succeeds but per-destination Status array must be inspected. Callers that do not check response.Status silently drop failed recipients.

1015.resolution: Rejected: ses-bulk-partial-destination-failure requires checking that response.Status is inspected after SendBulkTemplatedEmailCommand. This is a schema extension, not a current-cycle fix. Deferred pending return-value checker support.

1016.resolution: Rejected: SendCustomVerificationEmailCommand, CreateTemplateCommand, and UpdateTemplateCommand are all invoked via SESClient.send(), which the scanner already detects. The ses-send-no-try-catch postcondition applies to all commands passed to send(). No additional detection needed.

1172.description: Add detection for jszip JSZipObject.async() method calls — postcondition file-async-no-try-catch added in depth pass but no scanner rule exists for .async() method call pattern on JSZipObject instances

evidence.note: Proactive — contract added via API surface analysis. JSZipObject.async() is called in every zip file reading workflow after loadAsync(). Common pattern: zip.files["name"].async("string") without try-catch. Decompression via pako can throw on corrupted DEFLATE data even when the zip container passes loadAsync().

1172.resolution: Extended PropertyChainDetector.buildPropertyChain() to walk through ElementAccessExpression nodes when the inner expression is a PropertyAccessExpression. This enables detection of zip.files["name"].async(type) patterns (and zip.files[variable].async(type)) by treating bracket-index access as transparent in the property chain. The scanner now detects file-async-no-try-catch for direct JSZipObject.async() calls after bracket notation. Note: file.async() called on variables destructured from Object.entries(zip.files) cannot be detected (TypeScript-inferred type tracking not supported). Fixture annotations updated to reflect this limitation. Also fixed pre-existing @aws-sdk/client-ses and cloudinary contract schema validation errors (invalid incident_label, user_experience, visibility, incident_cost_range values).

1173.description: Add detection for jszip JSZipObject.async() unsupported type pattern — postcondition file-async-unsupported-type added in depth pass: callers using blob/uint8array type in Node.js environments throw unsupported platform error

evidence.note: Proactive — contract added via API surface analysis. Pattern: zip.files["name"].async("blob") in Node.js code throws Error: blob is not supported by this platform. Needs a separate detector from file-async-no-try-catch since the type-checking issue exists even WITH try-catch present.

1173.resolution: The file-async-unsupported-type postcondition is detected by the same mechanism as file-async-no-try-catch — both postconditions are on the same contract function (async). The property-chain fix in concern-1 covers detection for both postconditions. The scanner fires file-async-no-try-catch (error, higher severity) rather than file-async-unsupported-type (warning) when both apply, as contract-matcher picks the most severe postcondition.

2061.description: 25 ai sdk tool-execution-error violations marked false positive across 25 tool files. 2070.description: Add detection for mysql2 PreparedStatementInfo.close() missing call — postcondition prepared-statement-close-missing documents that not calling stmt.close() after connection.prepare() leaks server-side prepared statement slots. evidence.note: Proactive — source confirmed: mysql2/lib/promise/prepared_statement_info.js close() always resolves (fire-and-forget). (2) iswhitelisted-unchecked-return: detecting whether the boolean return of isWhitelisted is acted upon requires analyzing downstream usage of the return value, which the return-value-checker does not support for validator boolean-return functions. 2496.description: The undici contract concern `response-json-parse-error` flags `res.json()` as "Generic error handling found" even when the code has BOTH required layers: (1) an explicit `res.status === 200` or `res.ok` guard before calling `.json()`, and (2) a try-catch around `.json()` with specific `SyntaxError` inspection. The analyzer's control-flow checker sees the catch block but classifies it as "generic" because it does not detect `error.response.status` inspection inside the catch. However, for fetch/undici, the idiomatic pattern is to check `response.ok` or `response.status` BEFORE calling `.json()` (not inside the catch), and then catch JSON parse errors separately. The analyzer should recognize this two-layer pattern as compliant: status-guard-before-json + typed-catch-after-json. Currently it only recognizes the axios-style pattern where error inspection happens inside the catch block. This was discovered scanning nark's own codebase (`src/cli/auth.ts:76`) where the auth polling loop checks `res.status === 200` before `res.json()` and wraps the parse in `try { res.json() } catch (jsonErr) { if (jsonErr instanceof SyntaxError) ... }`. The violation was suppressed as a false positive.

details.current_behavior: Flags as WARNING with message: Generic error handling found. Consider inspecting error.response.status to distinguish between 4xx client errors and 5xx server errors.
details.expected_behavior: Should recognize res.ok/res.status guard before .json() call as compliant. The status-before-json pattern is the correct fetch/undici idiom, unlike axios where status is inspected inside the catch.
details.pattern_to_recognize: if (res.ok) { try { await res.json() } catch (e) { ... } } OR if (res.status === 200) { try { await res.json() } catch (e) { ... } }
details.root_cause: control-flow-analyzer classifies any catch block without error.response.status inspection as generic. It does not consider that the status was already checked in a parent if-condition before the .json() call site.
details.also_fixed: V2-to-V1 adapter (src/v2/adapter.ts) was not passing fingerprint field through convertViolation(), causing all V2 violations to have fingerprint:null in scan JSON output. Fixed by forwarding v2.fingerprint to the V1 violation object.

2497.description: The V2-to-V1 adapter in src/v2/adapter.ts was dropping the fingerprint field when converting V2 violations to V1 format. The V2 analyzer (contract-matcher.ts) computes fingerprints via computeViolationFingerprint() and stores them on each violation, but convertViolation() did not include the field in the returned V1 object. This caused all violations in .nark/scans/*.json to have fingerprint:null, which broke the suppression system (suppressions are keyed by fingerprint). The scan-writer had a fallback that recomputes fingerprints, but it mutated violation objects AFTER the scan JSON was already written. Fixed by forwarding v2.fingerprint through the adapter as (v1 as any).fingerprint = v2.fingerprint.

details.impact: All V2-generated violations had fingerprint:null in scan JSON, breaking suppressions add/verify workflow
details.fix_applied: Added fingerprint passthrough: if (v2.fingerprint) { (v1 as any).fingerprint = v2.fingerprint; }
details.note: V1 Violation interface in types.ts does not have a fingerprint field. The field is carried as an ad-hoc property. A proper fix would add fingerprint to the V1 Violation interface, but that is a broader change.

2497.resolution: Fixed in src/v2/adapter.ts convertViolation() — fingerprint now passed through from V2 to V1 violation objects.

2498.description: Extend telemetry to send suppression details and fix-vs-suppress resolution data. Currently telemetry sends suppressionCount (a number) but not WHY violations were suppressed. Adding suppression reasons, per-contract-clause fix/suppress ratios, and nark-fix agent resolution data would crowdsource false-positive detection from thousands of users. High suppress rates on a specific contract clause = likely FP or overly strict rule. Agent reasons explain WHY. This data feeds directly back into profile quality improvements. Three additions: (1) Include suppression details in scan telemetry — for each suppressed violation send { fingerprint, package, postconditionId, reason, suppressedBy }. (2) Add fix-vs-suppress ratio per contract clause — when a violation is resolved (code fix or suppression), track which path was taken. High suppress:fix ratio on a clause signals a profile quality issue. (3) Add nark-fix agent telemetry endpoint — when nark-fix resolves a violation, send { violationId, resolution: fixed|suppressed|skipped, agentReason: string, codeChangeSize: number }. This is the richest signal — the AI agent has already analyzed the code and determined whether the violation is real. Privacy: suppression reasons are about Nark profiles, not user code. Code snippets are already sent for authenticated users. Frame as: help improve Nark profiles — suppression reasons are sent anonymously to reduce false positives. Respect existing NARK_TELEMETRY=off and DO_NOT_TRACK=1 opt-outs.

proposed_new_fields.suppressionDetails: Array<{ fingerprint, package, postconditionId, reason, suppressedBy }>
proposed_new_fields.resolutionsByClause: Record<string, { fixed: number, suppressed: number, skipped: number }>

details.privacy_note: Suppression reasons describe Nark profile behavior, not user business logic. Same opt-out mechanisms apply (NARK_TELEMETRY=off, DO_NOT_TRACK=1).

Many React Query projects ship a global `new QueryCache({ onError: (error) => toast(...) })` wired into the queryClient at a separate file (e.g., `lib/query-client.ts`, `providers/QueryClientProvider.tsx`). 2717.description: Scanner flags bootstrapModule() called inside a .then(() => bootstrapModule(...)) callback that is itself joined to a chain with .catch(). Concretely: the canonical vendure pattern `loadAppConfig().then(() => platformBrowserDynamic().bootstrapModule(AppModule)).catch(err => ...)` flags the inner bootstrapModule call as missing handler even though the returned promise is propagated through the outer chain and caught by the outer .catch. hasCatchHandler() walks the immediate parent only — it sees the .then arrow body as the parent, which has no .catch sibling. Fix: when a node is the sole expression in an arrow function body that is itself the callback to a .then(), treat the outer .then().catch() chain as the relevant handler scope.

2717.resolution: Extended ControlFlowAnalysis.hasCatchHandler in nark/src/v2/core/control-flow-analyzer.ts with Pattern C — propagated-promise detection. 2777.resolution: Deferred: callback-error-flow tracking is a non-trivial scanner enhancement not yet implemented. The current sqlite3 contract uses the existing callback-error-ignored detection (see node_modules/sqlite3/lib/sqlite3.d.ts wrappers in contract.yaml), which fires on the common run()/get()/all()/exec()/prepare() patterns. Adding (a) constructor-callback detection (new sqlite3.Database(file, cb)), (b) Statement.get-specific callback-arg-ignored detection, and (c) Statement variable-flow lifecycle tracking (.finalize/.reset reachability) requires (1) extending callback-detector to walk constructor arguments, (2) per-method postcondition routing that distinguishes Database.get from Statement.get (same method name, different parent class), and (3) variable-lifetime flow analysis for prepared Statement instances. The existing callback-error-ignored postcondition already covers the most common silent-failure case (callback-based run/get/all/exec).

2780.resolution: Implemented: added pure-AST local-factory-function tracking to InstanceTrackerPlugin. New beforeTraversal pass walkLocalFactoryDeclarations() registers any top-level `const X = () => new <ImportedClass>(...)` or `function X() { return new <ImportedClass>(...) }` factory into a localFactoryMap. resolveFactoryCall() then consults this map as a fallback (after importMap and factoryToPackage) when handling direct-identifier calls. Pure AST — does not rely on the TypeScript type checker, so it works even when the underlying package is not installed in node_modules (the fixture case). Verified: nark-corpus-pro/packages/@umami/node/fixtures/instance-usage.ts now fires the expected 5 violations on functions trackOnInstance, trackInstanceFireAndForget, identifyOnInstance, identifyOnInstanceFireAndForget, sendOnInstance — all matching the SHOULD_FIRE expectations in the concern. The 3 safe baselines (.catch() chain, try-catch await, .catch only) correctly do NOT fire. No regressions: full umami ground-truth suite (14 tests) + instance-tracker.test.ts (8 tests) all pass. Also added detection.class_names: [Umami] to nark-corpus-pro/packages/@umami/node/contract.yaml so the classToPackage fallback resolves Umami when importMap misses (covers any future call sites where Umami is referenced without being directly imported in the same file).

2805.description: minio.Client field on a class (private minioClient!: Client) is not picked up by InstanceTrackerPlugin when accessed via `this.minioClient.<method>()` from a class private/instance method. Hypothesis: the definite-assignment `!:` field declaration form is not threaded through instance tracking, or the `this.<field>` resolution path is missing for fields whose type annotation is a registered class_names entry. Affects all packages using Client-class fields with instance methods (minio, @aws-sdk/*, @prisma/*, mongo, etc).
2805.fixture_required: A minimal repro fixture: class with `private client!: Client` field initialized in constructor + a private async method calling `await this.client.someMethod()` outside try-catch. Should produce a violation when this.client is resolvable to a minio.Client via type annotation.

Investigation: (1) Added a regression fixture to nark-corpus-pro/packages/minio/fixtures/ground-truth.ts mirroring the exact be-gateway-service pattern (class with `private minioClient!: Client` field, assigned in constructor via `this.minioClient = new Client(...)`, called as `await this.minioClient.bucketExists(bucket)` from both public and private async methods). (2) All 4 new test cases pass: 3 SHOULD_FIRE on bare-await calls (bucketExists, putObject in private method) and 1 SHOULD_NOT_FIRE on try-catch-wrapped call. (3) Full 22-test suite for minio passes. The detection path that handles this pattern: InstanceTrackerPlugin.beforeTraversal calls walkTypeAnnotations on every PropertyDeclaration with a type annotation; `Client` is in contract.detection.type_names and is confirmed via the file's importMap (import { Client } from 'minio'); the PropertyChainDetector's `this.member.method()` branch then resolves `minioClient` via instanceTracker.resolveIdentifier(). (4) Root-cause of the original be-gateway-scan miss: the scan file (work-packages/minio/real-world-scans/be-gateway-scan.json) shows `contracts_applied: 0`, meaning package discovery applied zero contracts during that scan — almost certainly because the test repo had no node_modules installed (TypeScript checker resolves every package call as `any`, package discovery fails, no contracts get applied). This is an environment / install issue, not a scanner detection gap. Regression fixture retained as guard against future regressions to walkTypeAnnotations / PropertyDeclaration handling.

2806.description: tencentcloud-sdk-nodejs has 255+ sub-product Client classes (cvm, vpc, tmt, cos, sms, ocr, ...) each extending AbstractClient. Sub-product Clients expose action-specific methods (DescribeZones, TextTranslateBatch, DescribeInstances, ...) that internally call this.request(action, req). The contract documents 3 top-level methods (request, requestOctetStream, getCredential) because those are the only methods named in official docs. The analyzer matches function calls by literal name, so the dominant real-world callsite pattern (subclass extends X Client; super.MethodName(req).then(...)) is missed entirely. Same issue affects @alicloud sub-products and similar API-generator-based SDKs. Fix: wildcard / catch-all detection on any async method called on a class instance imported from tencentcloud-sdk-nodejs/tencentcloud/services/**/v*/**_client paths.
2806.resolution: Deferred (not rejected on merit). The concern describes a real cross-package scanner gap: auto-generated SDK clients (tencentcloud-sdk-nodejs, @alicloud/*, similar API-generator SDKs) expose dozens of action-specific methods (TextTranslateBatch, DescribeZones, ...) on sub-Client subclasses, all internally routed to a contracted request() postcondition. Current analyzer cannot bind these action methods because (a) no class-extends tracking via HeritageClause exists in InstanceTracker, (b) no super.X() / this.X() handling exists inside subclass methods, and (c) no wildcard / catch-all mode exists in the contract schema. Implementation would require a new schema field (e.g. subclass_action_method_wildcard with deep-import-path regex + target function name), heritage-clause walking in InstanceTracker, and a new detector for super/this calls inside subclasses of contracted base classes. That is a substantial scanner architecture change (new plugin, schema migration, regression risk across 191 contracts). The evidence in this concern (1 repo, 1 expected violation) is below the skill threshold for an immediate scanner upgrade. Action taken: (1) added defensive regression fixture at nark-corpus-pro/packages/tencentcloud-sdk-nodejs/fixtures/subclass-wildcard-deferred.ts with @expect-violation annotations so the future implementation has a concrete test target, (2) deferred to a batched scanner-upgrade design once bc-fp-harvester surfaces the @alicloud and AWS SDK v2-style equivalents (>=3 distinct packages, >=3 distinct repos) so the schema + plugin design can be informed by the full cross-package surface, not just tencentcloud. Re-open as a new concern (or roll up into a batch backlog item) when threshold is met.

2807.description: When NARK_ALLOW_MISSING_DEPS=1 is set and node_modules is absent, bare named imports do not get routed through the contract matcher. ThrowingFunctionDetector.handleDirectCall at throwing-function-detector.ts:239 relies on context.importMap.get(identName), which appears to require a resolvable .d.ts to populate the binding. Result: real bare-import call sites (e.g. await unpackTar(buffer)) silently skip detection. The package-discovery layer DID detect modern-tar in the file (logs show "modern-tar: imported in 1 file(s)"), so the gap is in name-to-package binding during analysis, not in package discovery.

details.context: pnpm install was denied; tsconfig.app.json used; 13 files analyzed but bare named imports from modern-tar produced 0 detections
details.hypothesis: importMap is built by walking ts.SourceFile imports + resolving each via typeChecker. When deps are missing, typeChecker returns undefined symbols; the named-import entry is either skipped or its packageName falls back to undefined. Need to fall back to the literal import specifier text (e.g. "modern-tar") when symbol resolution fails, mirroring the symbol?.name ?? identifier.text pattern at line 236.

2807.resolution: The concern's hypothesis was wrong — the importMap binding works fine; the actual bug was in UniversalAnalyzer.initialize() (src/v2/analyzer.ts). The sxzz_typescript-go-playground tsconfig.app.json extends `@vue/tsconfig/tsconfig.dom.json`, which doesn't resolve when node_modules is absent. This triggered the synthetic-tsconfig fallback branch at lines 95-149. That branch created `this.program` correctly but then `return`ed early at line 148, skipping the ContractMatcher creation step at lines 175-182. Result: detections fired correctly (verified empirically — the throwing-function-detector produced `modern-tar | unpackTar | throwing-function | confidence: high` for the call site), but `this.contractMatcher` was undefined so `analyzeFile()` skipped matching at the `if (this.contractMatcher)` guard. Every scan that hit the missing-extends fallback produced 0 violations regardless of detector output. Fix: restructured initialize() so the fallback branch falls through to the shared ContractMatcher creation step instead of returning early. Added regression test src/v2/analyzer-tsconfig-fallback.test.ts with two cases (fallback path + normal path) — both verify `contractMatcher` is set post-initialize. Empirical verification: scanning sxzz_typescript-go-playground/tsconfig.app.json with NARK_ALLOW_MISSING_DEPS=1 now correctly fires the unpack-malformed-archive violation at src/core.ts:18.

2808.description: @nestjs/axios HttpService methods (get/post/put/patch/delete/head/request/postForm/putForm/patchForm) return Observable<AxiosResponse>, not Promise. Underlying axios errors propagate via subscriber.error(err). Callers MUST satisfy the contract using ONE of three RxJS-aware patterns: (1) await firstValueFrom(...) inside a try/catch — currently DETECTED correctly; (2) .pipe(catchError(...)) on the Observable chain — currently NOT recognized as satisfying the postcondition, producing 2 FPs in ground-truth fixture (lines 139, 147); (3) .subscribe({ next, error }) with non-null error handler — currently NOT recognized, producing 1 FP in ground-truth fixture (line 159). The scanner correctly detects all 10 SHOULD_FIRE cases (bare firstValueFrom without try/catch across get/post/put/patch/delete/head/request/postForm/putForm/patchForm) and 4 SHOULD_NOT_FIRE try/catch cases. Need to extend the V2 analyzer to recognize .pipe(catchError(...)) and .subscribe({error: nonNull}) as satisfying postconditions whose throws clause says 'AxiosError emitted via the Observable error channel'.

details.fp_pattern_1: httpService.get(url).pipe(map(...), catchError(...)) is flagged as get-error-4xx-5xx
details.fp_pattern_2: httpService.post(url, body).pipe(map(...), catchError(...)) is flagged as post-error-4xx-5xx
details.fp_pattern_3: httpService.post(url, body).subscribe({ next, error }) is flagged as post-error-4xx-5xx
details.tp_pattern: await firstValueFrom(httpService.X(...)) without try/catch is correctly flagged
details.tn_pattern: await firstValueFrom(httpService.X(...)) inside try/catch is correctly not flagged
details.proposed_fix: When a contract postcondition's 'throws' field contains 'Observable error channel' or contract.detection.instance_chain_methods covers the verb, walk the call expression's parents: (a) if wrapped in a .pipe() whose arguments include catchError, suppress the violation; (b) if the call is followed by .subscribe({...}) and the argument object has a non-null 'error' property, suppress the violation. These check the RxJS error-handling channel just as try/catch around firstValueFrom checks the Promise rejection channel.

2809.description: Stream iteration consumer detection. The @langchain/langgraph contract codifies a 'stream-iteration-no-try-catch' postcondition: when `const stream = await graph.stream(...)` is wrapped in try-catch but the subsequent `for await (const chunk of stream)` consumer loop is NOT inside that same try, mid-stream errors (GraphRecursionError after N supersteps, NodeTimeoutError, LLM rate-limit errors thrown by a node mid-graph) surface during iteration and are uncaught. The analyzer currently fires on the `await graph.stream(...)` call site itself (when bare) but does NOT detect the pattern of `for await (... of trackedStreamVar)` outside try. To support this postcondition, the V2 analyzer needs to (a) track that `streamVar` returned from `graph.stream()` is a tracked-package awaitable stream, and (b) emit a violation when the `ForOfStatement` with await is not enclosed in a try-catch. The same gap likely affects @langchain/openai's stream-iteration-error postcondition (already filed as a known scanner limitation in that contract).

repos: langchain-ai/openwork (correct pattern: outer try wraps stream + consumer)

details.ground_truth_annotation: currently SHOULD_NOT_FIRE pending scanner support; flip to SHOULD_FIRE once detector lands
details.proposed_fix: Extend the InstanceTrackerPlugin or add a new ForAwaitConsumerDetector plugin: when `const stream = await trackedVar.stream(...)` resolves to a contracted package's stream method, record `stream` as a stream-iterating instance. Then walk ForOfStatement nodes with `awaitModifier`: when the iterable identifier is a recorded stream-iterating instance AND the ForOfStatement is not enclosed in a TryStatement, emit a violation pointing at the corresponding postcondition (e.g. stream-iteration-no-try-catch). Requires a per-contract opt-in flag (e.g. detection.stream_methods: ['stream']) so we only fire on packages where the stream iteration is the canonical error vector. Reuses the existing try-catch enclosure check from ContractMatcher.

2810.description: InstanceTrackerPlugin.resolveSchemaChainFactory() walks call/property chains to find the root identifier and resolve it to a package via importMap. Builder-style APIs that route through `new ClassName(...).method().method().compile()` have a NewExpression at the chain root, not an identifier — previously the loop exited with current = NewExpression and returned null, so the chained instance was untracked. Extended the chain walker to accept NewExpression as a root and resolve via importMap / classToPackage. 2811.description: Scanner does not treat `return X(...)` (where X is a contracted throwing function returning Promise) as ownership-pass to the caller. Helper functions that proxy a throwing call via direct return are flagged as violations even though the rejection is intentionally surfaced to the helper's caller. Generic pattern, not exponential-backoff-specific — affects any contract whose required_handling allows return-passthrough.

details.precision_impact: Bumped exponential-backoff real-world precision from 100% to 91.7% (1 FP of 12)

2812.description: Scanner flags throwing contracted function calls inside React Query / TanStack Query / SWR queryFn bodies even though the surrounding library auto-catches the throw and exposes it via isError/error. Generic pattern — affects every async throw contract (graphql-request, axios, prisma, fetch wrappers, etc). queryFn signature: `queryFn: () => contractedThrowingCall()` or `queryFn: async () => contractedThrowingCall()`.

details.package_affected: graphql-request (but generic to all throw-contract packages)
details.precision_impact: graphql-request real-world precision: 1/7 = 14% on pezzo+nhost — would be 100% (1/1) if queryFn-body suppression applied. Same FP class likely on @apollo/client, axios, openai, etc.

2813.description: Scanner-level FP: when a package contract registers a generic-named method like "extend" in detection.factory_methods, the scanner fires the postcondition on ANY call to ".extend()" — including calls on unrelated objects with their own .extend() method (e.g. a menu-item builder, a query builder, a lodash chain). Example surfaced during ky onboarding: RSSNext/Folo apps/desktop/layer/renderer/src/atoms/context-menu.ts:153 — "nextItem.extend({ click: ... })" fired ky inherited-http-error even though nextItem is a custom MenuItem type, not a ky instance. Fix direction: scope factory_methods to confirmed instances of the package (i.e. only fire on default-import.extend() or on a tracked instance variable), instead of any bare .extend() call.

details.example_pattern: nextItem.extend({...}) on a custom MenuItem type
details.package_affected: ky (could affect any contract that registers a common method name like extend/create/from)
details.precision_impact: ky real-world precision on Folo dropped from 1.0 to 0.0 on a single-violation repo; on agentic precision is unaffected because the contract is intended to cover all SDK wrappers there.

2814.description: Scanner anchors lock-unhandled-rejection to the lockfile.lock() call expression rather than the await site. When code splits into `const p = lockfile.lock(...); try { await p } catch {...}`, the call expression is flagged even though the awaited promise IS handled in try-catch 7 lines later.

evidence.pattern: separated promise creation + later awaited consumption inside try-catch
evidence.real_code: const lockPromise = lockfile.lock(resourcePath, {...}); try { releaseLock = await lockPromise } catch (err) {...}

2814.resolution: Pending: Detector should follow variable bindings — if the lock() call is assigned to a variable, only flag if no later await on that variable is wrapped in try-catch. Generalizes to any await_pattern detector.

2815.description: Reinforces concern-20260616-return-passthrough-not-recognized. 2816.description: Scanner does not track renamed bindings when a function is imported with an `as` rename. details.workaround: Authors must avoid renaming the imported binding; or detection_plugin must track the imported-symbol -> local-name aliasing across the AST

2990.description: Add factory-of-binding tracking so the scanner can distinguish `cosmiconfig()` explorer instances (async, current target — search/load return Promises) from `cosmiconfigSync()` instances (sync, NEW target — search/load throw synchronously). The same method names (`search` / `load`) are exposed by both, so without tracking which factory the binding came from, the scanner either over-flags (false positives on sync calls in CLI startup paths that legitimately handle sync throws via try-catch but don't await) or under-flags (misses the new search-sync postcondition). Recommended detection shape: walk the binding's RHS expression chain; if it's `cosmiconfigSync(...)` (or returns the result of such a call), tag the explorer with `factory: 'sync'` and route method calls (`.search()`, `.load()`) through sync-rule processing. The new search-sync postcondition needs sync-throw detection (caller MUST wrap call site in try-catch — no `.catch()` chain works because there is no Promise).

evidence.note: Proactive — postcondition added via API surface analysis. Real-world cosmiconfigSync usage common in CLI tools (e.g. stylelint, postcss, prettier all use both async and sync factories conditionally).

2991.description: Companion to concern-20260619-cosmiconfig-deepen-1 — same factory-of-binding tracking is required for `explorerSync.load(path)`. The sync load() method throws synchronously on missing file (ENOENT), unreadable file (EACCES), or parse error (loader Error with .filepath set since v9). Unlike sync search() (which silently retries fs errors while walking the directory tree), sync load() throws on EVERY failure mode — there is no null short-circuit. Detection should require try-catch around the sync call expression (no `await`); the existing async-load postcondition's `await` requirement does not apply to the sync surface. Until this lands, the new load-sync-throws-on-missing-or-malformed-file postcondition documents the contract obligation but is not actively detected.

2992.description: Add detection for bcrypt.getRounds(hash) — synchronous throwing function. Throws Error('Illegal arguments: ' + typeof hash) when hash is not a string (source: bcryptjs@3.0.3 index.js:296-300). Common production path: callers compute the cost factor of a stored hash to decide whether to rehash on login; if the user record was not found the hash is undefined and getRounds throws synchronously, surfacing into the login handler. Detection shape: require try-catch around any direct call to `bcrypt.getRounds(...)` or `getRounds(...)` (named import). Cannot rely on `await` — function is sync. Also surface the silent-NaN edge case via a separate weak-warning rule: a comparison like `getRounds(h) < N` where the result is not first checked for NaN may silently never rehash weak hashes (this is a security-degradation pattern, not a throw, so a separate rule from the main type-error rule).

evidence.note: Proactive — postcondition added via API surface analysis at pass 18 (2026-06-19). getRounds is the canonical signal for transparent password upgrade flows in production auth (e.g. NextAuth, Auth.js, Lucia).

2993.description: Add detection for bcrypt.getSalt(hash) — synchronous throwing function with TWO distinct throw modes. Throws Error('Illegal arguments: ' + typeof hash) when hash is not a string, AND throws Error('Illegal hash length: ' + length + ' != 60') when hash is a string but length !== 60 (source: bcryptjs@3.0.3 index.js:308-314). The illegal-length throw is the production-relevant one: bcrypt hashes stored in a VARCHAR column narrower than 60 (a common schema mistake — VARCHAR(40) was inherited from older MD5-style auth tables) silently truncate on write but THROW on read. The compareSync silent-false-on-bad-hash bug and the getSalt illegal-length throw share a root cause but have opposite UX (silent vs explicit) — both need detection. Detection shape: require try-catch around any direct call to `bcrypt.getSalt(...)`. Single rule covers both type-error and illegal-length throws since the syntactic position is identical.

evidence.note: Proactive — postcondition added via API surface analysis at pass 18 (2026-06-19). getSalt is rarely called in modern code (compare() is preferred) but the illegal-length throw is a high-signal indicator of database-schema drift.

2994.description: Add detection for bcrypt.truncates(password) — synchronous throwing function used as preflight check before hash/hashSync. Throws Error('Illegal arguments: ' + typeof password) if password is not a string (source: bcryptjs@3.0.3 index.js:322-326). The throw itself is mostly self-resolving (callers either validate the input first or wrap the call); the bigger contract concern is the SECONDARY rule: a call to `bcrypt.truncates(pw)` whose result is discarded or only logged, followed by `bcrypt.hash(pw, ...)` on the same password, is a no-op preflight — the function exists specifically to make the caller decide whether to reject the password, not to bypass the truncation. Detection shape: (1) basic — require try-catch around any direct `truncates(...)` call (covers the throw); (2) advanced (future) — flag the `truncates(pw); ... hash(pw)` pattern where the result of truncates is not branched on.

evidence.note: Proactive — postcondition added via API surface analysis at pass 18 (2026-06-19). The advanced detection (preflight-without-branch) is a UX/security pattern, not a throw — file as a separate priority once the basic rule lands.

Same control-flow shape needed for several other test-cleanup contracts (mock.verify(), spy.restore(), etc.) - this concern is the canonical starting point for a verify-then-restore detector family. Often a true-positive - even experienced sinon users miss the try/finally requirement on bare verify(), as evidenced by stale issues in sinonjs/sinon (e.g. #1673 family).

3081.description: Add detection for sandbox.verifyAndRestore() inside a try/catch where the catch block is empty or swallows the error without re-throw or recorder call. Swallowed ExpectationError means failing mock contracts pass CI undetected - the verifiable production behavior is no longer verified. Detection shape: `try { <sandbox>.verifyAndRestore(); } catch { /* empty */ }` or `catch (e) { /* no use of e, no throw */ }`. Postcondition: verify-and-restore-expectation-throws.

evidence.note: Proactive - contract added via API surface analysis during deepen-stream-3 pass 10 (2026-06-23) against sinon@22.0.0. Severity: error. Detection requires recognizing an empty catch block (no statements) or a catch block whose only statements are non-rethrow no-ops (console.log without throw, ignored variables). Same shape as a general 'swallowed error' detector, but scoped to verifyAndRestore calls. This is a SILENT_FAILURE - silently swallowed ExpectationErrors will let broken mock contracts pass CI for months.

3082.description: Add detection for sinon.restoreObject(value) where value's static type includes undefined or null (e.g. `let target: { method: () => string } | undefined; sinon.restoreObject(target);`) and the call is not guarded by a truthy check OR wrapped in try/catch. sinon throws `Error: Trying to restore object but received <stringified-falsy>` on falsy input. Detection shape: `sinon.restoreObject(<expr>)` where TypeScript flow analysis determines <expr>'s type is possibly nullish AND the call is not inside an `if (<expr>) { ... }` guard or try/catch block. Postcondition: restore-object-falsy-input-throws.

evidence.note: Proactive - contract added via API surface analysis during deepen-stream-3 pass 10 (2026-06-23) against sinon@22.0.0. Severity: error. Detection requires TypeScript-aware flow analysis (or a simpler heuristic: check if the argument identifier was declared with explicit `| undefined` / `| null` annotation, or assigned from a function returning nullish). FP rate may be moderate if non-typed JS is common in the corpus - restrict initially to TS-typed callsites where the argument's type union includes undefined/null. Same shape as other null-arg-throw detectors (e.g. fs.readFileSync(undefined) family).

3083.description: Add detection for prisma.<model>.aggregate({ _sum/_min/_max/_avg: { field: true } }) where the returned aggregate field is used in arithmetic or comparison without a null-check. Prisma's aggregate returns null for _sum/_min/_max/_avg fields when zero rows match the where clause, NOT 0 or undefined. Static analysis cannot determine match-count, so any aggregate-field property access that doesn't traverse a null-narrowing branch is a likely runtime crash. Detection shape: `<expr>.<_sum|_min|_max|_avg>.<field>` where <expr> is the result of an aggregate() call AND there is no preceding null check (?., ??, if-narrowing, optional chaining) AND the property is consumed in arithmetic (`+`, `-`, `*`, `/`), comparison (`>`, `<`, `===`), or non-nullish-coalescing assignment. Postcondition: aggregate-null-when-no-rows.

evidence.note: Proactive - contract added via API surface analysis during deepen-stream-2 pass 13 (2026-06-23) against @prisma/client@7.8.0. Severity: error. This is one of Prisma's highest-impact silent-failure patterns: revenue dashboards, financial sums, and analytics queries routinely consume `_sum.amount` directly. _count is the only aggregate field that returns 0 (not null) on no-rows - all others return null. Detection should be conservative (only flag aggregate->property->arithmetic chains) to keep FP rate manageable. High value: this pattern silently corrupts financial calculations (PAYMENT_RISK incident label).

3084.description: Add detection for prisma.$queryRawUnsafe(...) and prisma.$executeRawUnsafe(...) calls where the first argument is NOT a string literal or no-substitution template literal. These methods are documented as 'unsafe' - the SQL string bypasses Prisma's parameterization. The recommended safe form is to pass user-supplied values via the second-arg array (`...params`), keeping the SQL string a literal. Detection shape: `<prisma>.$queryRawUnsafe(<expr>, ...)` or `<prisma>.$executeRawUnsafe(<expr>, ...)` where <expr> is NOT a StringLiteral or TemplateLiteral with no expressions. Severity should be error - this is a SQL injection vector. Postcondition: queryrawunsafe-sql-injection / executerawunsafe-sql-injection.

evidence.note: Proactive - contract added via API surface analysis during deepen-stream-2 pass 13 (2026-06-23) against @prisma/client@7.8.0. Severity: error. SECURITY_RISK / critical incident cost. This is a security-relevant gap previously deferred in v1.1.0 deepen pass. Detection is mechanical: type-check the first argument. If it's a binary-plus expression, template literal with substitutions, or any non-literal identifier reference, flag it. The recommended fix is to convert all interpolated values into positional params. Note: a TemplateLiteral with no substitutions is safe (equivalent to a string literal).

3085.description: Add detection for prisma.<model>.createManyAndReturn(...) and prisma.<model>.updateManyAndReturn(...) calls inside code that may target MySQL, MongoDB, or SQL Server. Both methods are PostgreSQL/CockroachDB/SQLite only - they throw at runtime on unsupported providers because those engines don't support RETURNING. Detection is non-trivial without schema introspection. Initial heuristic: flag every <model>.createManyAndReturn() / <model>.updateManyAndReturn() call site and require it be inside a try/catch that catches PrismaClientValidationError or runtime errors. Long-term: read the provider from prisma/schema.prisma if available. Postcondition: createmanyandreturn-unsupported-provider / updatemanyandreturn-unsupported-provider.

evidence.note: Proactive - contract added via API surface analysis during deepen-stream-2 pass 13 (2026-06-23) against @prisma/client@7.8.0. Severity: error. These methods are newer additions (v5.14.0 for createManyAndReturn, v6.2.0 for updateManyAndReturn) and adoption is growing. Their try/catch-less use is a likely portability bug for anyone deploying on MySQL or SQL Server. Pair with auto-detection of schema provider when available (Phase 2 enhancement).

3086.description: Add detection for prisma.<model>.findMany() where the result array is indexed (`result[0]`, `result[N]`) or non-empty-mapped (`result[0].field`, `result.find(...).field`) without an explicit empty-array guard (`if (result.length === 0)`, `if (!result.length)`, optional chaining). findMany returns [] silently on no-match - indexing an empty array yields undefined, and `.field` of undefined throws TypeError. Detection shape: `<prisma>.<model>.findMany(...)` -> assigned to <id> -> later `<id>[N].<prop>` access without preceding length-check. Postcondition: findmany-empty-array-not-checked.

evidence.note: Proactive - contract added via API surface analysis during deepen-stream-2 pass 13 (2026-06-23) against @prisma/client@7.8.0. Severity: warning. Scanner should flag the no-try-catch case so handlers explicitly differentiate retriable (401/JWT refresh) vs non-retriable (403/404/422) failures.

evidence.note: Proactive — postcondition added in deepen pass 47 (2026-06-24, deepen-stream-2). Existing generic RequestError detector likely covers the no-try-catch case; a future rule could distinguish JWT-expired (retriable) from installation-suspended (non-retriable) at the catch-block level.

3227.description: Add detection for octokit.repos.compareCommitsWithBasehead() — 404 deleted ref, 422 unrelated history, 403 oversized diff. Deploy preview and changelog bots break silently when uncaught. Existing 404 handling around getContent applies to read-only repo data; this method has an additional 403 large-diff failure mode that should hint at paginated fallback in the required handling.

evidence.note: Proactive — postcondition added in deepen pass 47 (2026-06-24, deepen-stream-2). No-try-catch detection inherited from existing octokit instance-method rule; the large-diff 403 fallback (paginated fetch) is a hint-only refinement, not a hard detection requirement.

3228.description: Add detection for octokit.issues.removeLabel() — dominant failure is 404-race between concurrent label automations. Stale-bot deployments at scale repeatedly crash mid-loop when two automations remove the same label. Scanner should flag no-try-catch and recommend treating 404 as no-op (desired end state); 410 (issue deleted) requires removing the issue from the queue.

evidence.note: Proactive — postcondition added in deepen pass 47 (2026-06-24, deepen-stream-2). Existing octokit await-pattern detector should pick this up; the 404-as-no-op semantic is a documentation-level hint for the suggested catch body, not a new scanner primitive.

3229.description: Add detection for octokit.pulls.dismissReview() — 422 when already dismissed (race), 403 when branch protection forbids non-admin dismissal, 404 when review or PR gone. Auto-dismiss-on-push and compliance reset automations break silently. Recommend 422 as no-op, 403 surfaced to operator (policy mismatch, not retriable).

evidence.note: Proactive — postcondition added in deepen pass 47 (2026-06-24, deepen-stream-2). The branch-protection-403 case is hard to model statically; a hint-only suggestion in the catch-body recommendation is sufficient for now.

3233.description: Add detection rule for sqs-send-batch-invalid-entry-id postcondition. SendMessageBatchCommand (and the same-shape DeleteMessageBatchCommand / ChangeMessageVisibilityBatchCommand) throws InvalidBatchEntryId synchronously when entry.Id doesn't match [A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,80}. Common bug: callers pass database UUIDs containing dots / slashes, or upstream message IDs with ':' or '/'. The ENTIRE batch is rejected — none of the messages are sent. Detection should flag batch-send call sites where Entry.Id is sourced from a string variable without an upstream replace/sanitize/match call. Lower-precision alternative: flag any SendMessageBatchCommand callsite that doesn't have a regex test or sanitize call in the Entries.map() body. Heuristic could check for the literal characters '.', '/', ':' in inline Id values.

evidence.note: Proactive — postcondition added by bc-deepen-contract 2026-06-24, no scanner rule yet. Existing batch postconditions (sqs-send-batch-no-try-catch, sqs-send-batch-failed-not-checked) cover the request-level and partial-failure cases. This new postcondition covers the synchronous-throw path on malformed entry IDs which is distinct and not covered by the umbrella try-catch heuristic (developers often wrap in try-catch but log-and-swallow without sanitizing IDs).
